I am an old man now, 76 years, and my strength is not what it was. On this maize plot here in Mbeya, I intercrop with beans as we always have done, and I use the manure from my few cattle because chemical fertilizer has become too costly for a small farmer like me. I will plant the seed I saved from last season — the hybrid seed from the shops is expensive and I cannot buy new every year. My sons and grandchildren help me with the heavy work of ploughing and weeding, and when the maize is ready I will pay some young men from the village to help with harvesting.
